🔻 Iran says Oman acts in good faith in talks on Strait of Hormuz

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei says Oman has acted in good faith during recent talks on shipping security in the Strait of Hormuz.

In his weekly press briefing on Monday, Baqaei stressed that Iran assumes the two littoral states will take their own interests into account.
​
He added that Oman, as a neighboring coastal country with long‑standing and very good relations with Iran, has acted in good faith throughout the process.
​
It remains to be seen what conditions will emerge in the next stages, said the official.
​
Baqaei also noted that the understanding between Iran and Oman is a necessary condition for ensuring security along the Strait of Hormuz’s shipping routes, but it is not sufficient on its own.
​
The spokesperson stressed that insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz stems from US and Israeli military aggression, which still continues, preventing vessels from transiting the waterway with confidence and security.

Even the everyday objects we pass by without a second thought become images when seen through Andy Warhol’s camera. Saint Laurent Rive Droite presents Andy Warhol’s photography exhibition <Banal Objects> in Seoul, curated by Anthony Vaccarello. Centered around Polaroid photographs created in the late 1970s, the exhibition captures familiar and ordinary objects through Warhol’s unique perspective, offering a new view of art, popular culture, and consumption.
The immediate, unretouched quality of Polaroid photographs meets everyday objects, allowing visitors to take a closer look at the world as Warhol saw it. Saint Laurent friends in Seoul also joined the occasion. CORTIS’ MARTIN, RIIZE’s ANTON, OLDEF’s ANNE, AHN HYO SEOP, CHA JUNG WON, LEE CHAE MIN, KIM DO YEON, and KIM NA YOUNG visited the exhibition and encountered Warhol’s perspective.
Andy Warhol’s everyday world, seen once again through Saint Laurent’s lens. Following Seoul, the exhibition will continue at Rive Droite Beijing.

⚡️ Iran-Pakistan chamber seeks free trade deal amid tariff hike

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The head of the Iran-Pakistan Joint Chamber says the chamber is negotiating to remove trade barriers following Pakistan’s recent increase in tariffs on some Iranian exports.

Abdolhakim Rigi-Mirjaveh said on Monday that the exact affected products and the new tariff rates need clarification, noting that preferential trade agreements cover some goods.
​
He warned that higher tariffs could raise export costs and reduce the competitiveness of Iranian goods in Pakistan.
​
Rigi-Mirjaveh said the chamber is pursuing a free trade agreement, which he said could significantly reduce tariff barriers and provide a more transparent and predictable trading environment.
​
He also called for the swift resolution of the situation involving trucks stranded at the Pishin border, stressing that the tariff hike does not constitute a trade ban.
